what_it_is.summary: This is a small Llama-style decoder, the layout used by many current open models, which comes with rotary positions, RMS normalisation and a gated feed-forward layer built in: 2 layers stacked one on another, each word held as a list of 128 numbers, 4 attention heads looking at the text in parallel. It reads at most 128 words at a time; anything earlier is invisible to it. It departs from the standard GPT-2 layout in 3 places, explained below.

components.name: Family
components.label: llama
components.plain: a small Llama-style decoder, the layout used by many current open models, which comes with rotary positions, RMS normalisation and a gated feed-forward layer built in

components.name: Attention
components.label: full
components.plain: every word can look back at every earlier word it can see (full attention)
components.technical: the softmax-normalised query-key similarities that mix values

components.name: Word positions
components.label: rotary
components.plain: word positions are encoded by rotating internal vectors (rotary positions), so the model sees how far apart two words are rather than where each one sits
components.technical: the function of index that tells attention where tokens are

components.name: Normalisation
components.label: RMSNorm
components.plain: each word's internal numbers are rescaled by their overall size only (RMS normalisation), a slightly cheaper way of keeping them in a stable range

components.name: Feed-forward switch
components.label: SwiGLU
components.plain: the feed-forward layers use a gate (SwiGLU) that lets one set of features switch another on or off, as most modern models do
components.technical: the per-token feed-forward block, read as a key-value memory

components.name: Layer shortcuts
components.label: residual
components.plain: each layer adds its result on top of what came in, so information can pass straight through (a residual shortcut)
components.technical: the additive skip pathway every block writes into

components.name: Optimiser
components.label: AdamW
components.plain: trained with AdamW, the standard optimiser, which adjusts each weight with its own step size
components.technical: the per-parameter moment estimates kept during training

what_to_expect.summary: Short small-talk replies for a handful of everyday topics: greetings, how are you, food, drinks, weather, hobbies, pets, outings, invitations and goodbyes. On 18 small-talk questions it answered most on topic (14 of 18): 9 of 10 when phrased as in training, 5 of 8 when reworded. Rewording a question makes it noticeably worse, so it is matching familiar phrasing more than understanding. Reliable here: greetings, how are you, favourite food, what did you do, the weather, hobbies, goodbyes. Never on topic here: invitations. It failed all 6 questions outside its training (facts, maths, remembering what you said, instructions), as expected.
can: reply on topic to greetings, how are you, favourite food, what did you do, the weather, hobbies, goodbyes
sometimes reply on topic to offering a drink, pets
